name: Saint Jane Frances de Chantal
history: A Burgundian baroness, wife and mother, widowed at twenty-eight when her husband was killed in a hunting accident. Under the direction of Saint Francis de Sales she grew in holiness and in 1610 founded with him the Order of the Visitation at Annecy, open to women whose age or health kept them from stricter orders.
life: Jane Frémyot married Christophe de Rabutin, Baron de Chantal, in 1592, and they were happy together. Four of their children survived infancy. In 1601 Christophe was shot by accident while hunting and died, and Jane, grief-stricken, struggled for years to forgive the man responsible, until at last she stood godmother to his child. In 1604 she heard Francis de Sales preach in Dijon and placed herself under his direction. He taught her a gentle, steady holiness in place of anxiety. In 1610 they founded the Visitation at Annecy. Leaving home was hard; her teenage son, the story goes, lay across the threshold to stop her, and she stepped over him in tears. The order spread quickly, and by her death there were over eighty houses. After Francis died in 1622, Saint Vincent de Paul became her friend and counsellor. She died at Moulins in 1641 and was canonised in 1767.
prayerTo: Saint Jane Frances, you knew the joys of marriage and the grief of losing your husband, and you learned to forgive. Pray for widows and for all who mourn, for those who cannot yet forgive, and for me, that I may serve God with a steady and gentle heart. Amen.
penance: Pray for someone who has hurt you today and, if it is safe and right, take one small step towards reconciliation.
meditation: Francis de Sales taught her to do everything by love and nothing by force. Where are you trying to force holiness instead of letting God lead you gently?
